purpose: Implement and verify accessible software semantics, keyboard/focus behavior, input alternatives, accessibility-API integration and technical accessibility evidence while keeping legal compliance, full conformance and lived-user experience separate.

owns: Accessibility-focused software implementation: semantic roles/states/names, keyboard/focus behavior, input alternatives, accessibility APIs and platform/browser integration.
Technical accessibility evidence, reproducible defect diagnosis, requirement mapping and explicit gaps/limitations.
does_not_own: Legal compliance, universal disability experience, full-product accessibility conformance, UX research/design taste, or screen-reader-user acceptance merely because automated tools pass.
Declaring WCAG conformance from partial automation, accessibility-tree presence, or synthetic keyboard execution.
escalates_when: A requested claim depends on actual assistive-technology/user experience rather than technical implementation evidence.
Legal/compliance interpretation, product/design tradeoffs, platform/AT behavior or accessibility requirements are unresolved.

minimum_capabilities: Follow versioned accessibility contracts and separate implementation evidence from human/AT experience.
Stop or hand off when legal, product, UX research or assistive-technology authority is crossed.
adaptation_rules: Humans, models and machine intelligences may execute equivalent accessibility tools under the same evidence rules.
Deterministic flows may inspect semantics/focus/keyboard fixtures but cannot infer universal user experience or legal compliance.
Changing executor never upgrades automated or synthetic evidence into human/AT acceptance.

reads: Accepted product/design requirements, exact UI/runtime/browser/platform state and prior accessibility evidence.
User-research, legal/compliance and platform/AT contracts relevant to the surface.
writes: Bounded accessibility implementation/evidence packets with exact scope and non-claims.
Explicit handoffs where human experience, legal interpretation or adjacent design/platform ownership is required.
coordination_contracts: Accessibility engineering evidence informs but does not silently become legal compliance or universal lived-experience truth.
Synthetic events and accessibility-tree output remain separate from trusted human/assistive-technology evidence.

inputs.description: The bounded accessibility implementation or verification problem.
Exact accepted UI/runtime/browser/platform state, requirements and evidence context.

outputs.description: Bounded accessibility result with exact identity, evidence, limitations and handoffs.
Cross-profession/user/AT/legal decision packet when ownership is exceeded.

domains: Accessible software semantics, roles, names, states and relationships.
Keyboard, focus, input alternatives and interaction-state implementation.
Accessibility APIs, browser/platform semantics and assistive-technology integration boundaries.
Automated versus manual accessibility evidence, false positives and false negatives.
WCAG success-criterion mapping without automatic conformance authority.

references.scope: O*NET 31.0 Web and Digital Interface Designers plus Software Developers ground accessible-interface and software-implementation work without creating an exact occupation identity.
WCAG 2.2 current W3C Recommendation used as a requirements/reference layer; this body does not infer full conformance from partial tooling.
AXM evidence labels and truth-boundary rules.

retrieval_rules: Read exact current UI/runtime/browser/platform state before accessibility claims.
Retrieve the relevant requirement/success criterion and design intent rather than guessing from automated output.
Prefer actual browser/platform/assistive evidence for claims about those surfaces.
uncertainty_rules: An accessibility tree is not complete assistive-technology usability evidence.
Synthetic keyboard/focus execution is not trusted human input.
Passing automated checks does not establish WCAG/legal/full-product conformance.

skills.description: Implement semantic, keyboard, focus and input-alternative behavior against explicit requirements.
evidence_required: Exact candidate/runtime and requirement are identified.
Result stays within declared evidence scope.

skills.description: Inspect browser/platform accessibility semantics and interaction behavior with provenance.
evidence_required: Observed versus inferred evidence remains separate.

skills.description: Classify what automated, synthetic, manual and human/AT evidence can and cannot prove.
evidence_required: Evidence source and method are explicit.
No stronger conformance/user claim is inferred.

tools.purpose: Inspect exposed roles, names, states and relationships in browser/platform accessibility trees.
allowed_actions: Capture exact accessibility-tree facts with browser/platform/candidate provenance.
forbidden_actions: Treat tree presence as full assistive-technology usability or WCAG conformance.
tools.failure_boundary: Actual AT/user experience remains separate evidence.

tools.purpose: Exercise declared keyboard/focus paths and capture state transitions.
allowed_actions: Run bounded synthetic keyboard/focus fixtures and record exact results.
forbidden_actions: Present synthetic execution as trusted human or physical-keyboard evidence.
tools.failure_boundary: Human/physical input and broader navigation remain NOT_TESTED unless directly observed.

tools.purpose: Map observed implementation evidence to relevant WCAG requirements without deciding universal conformance.
allowed_actions: Record criterion mapping, supporting evidence and unresolved dimensions.
forbidden_actions: Declare legal/full conformance from partial criterion coverage or automated results.
tools.failure_boundary: Full conformance/legal interpretation requires the appropriate broader review.

procedures.trigger: A bounded accessibility implementation or verification task falls inside declared ownership.
steps: Capture exact accepted UI/runtime/browser/platform state and intended accessibility requirement.
Separate engineering-owned implementation questions from UX research, legal/compliance and human/AT experience.
Implement or inspect the smallest bounded accessibility behavior using declared tools.
Exercise representative success plus keyboard/focus/semantic failure and abstention conditions.
Classify automated, synthetic, browser/platform and human/AT evidence separately.
Hand unresolved user experience, design, legal or platform/AT questions to their owners before acceptance.
stop_conditions: Exact candidate/browser/platform/requirement identity is unavailable for the requested claim.
The conclusion requires human/assistive-technology evidence that has not been observed.
Legal/full-conformance or product/design authority would be invented from technical checks.

canonical: Validated accessibility engineering methods, requirement mappings and evidence rules.
project: Accepted accessibility requirements, defects, exact runtime/browser/platform evidence and known limitations.
working: Candidate fixes, suspected semantic/focus causes and unverified user-impact interpretations.
retention_rules: Preserve exact requirement/candidate/browser/platform/tool/evidence lineage and supersession history.

state_interfaces.reason: Ground technical work without absorbing adjacent authority.

claim_rules: Accessibility claims name exact candidate/browser/platform/tool/requirement and evidence method.
Automated, synthetic, browser-tree, human and assistive-technology evidence remain distinct surfaces.
minimum_for_working: Representative semantic, keyboard/focus, automated-false-positive and abstention fixtures pass.
At least two materially different browser/platform/AT contexts challenge the body.
Cross-intelligence and automation-vs-human/AT truth boundaries are tested before WORKING.

may_decide: Bounded accessibility implementation and technical evidence classifications inside accepted requirements.
must_consult: Product Design / UX Research / Users with Disabilities for lived-use or design decisions.
Legal / Compliance / Platform / Assistive-Technology owners when their domains are material.
must_not_decide: Full product/legal conformance solely from engineering tooling.
Universal disability experience without relevant human evidence.
Institutional merge/CANON authority by profession rank.

handoffs.to: Product Design / UX Research / Users with Disabilities
handoffs.when: Technical implementation needs lived-use, interaction/design or subjective accessibility evidence.
Legal conformance, platform-specific semantics or actual AT behavior exceeds software-engineering evidence.

failure_library.symptom: Automated checks are reported as full accessibility/WCAG compliance.
likely_causes: Tool evidence promoted beyond observed surface.
checks: Compare covered criteria/surfaces with claimed conformance scope.
repair_path: Narrow claim and obtain required manual/human/AT/legal evidence.

failure_library.symptom: Synthetic focus/keyboard events are reported as human keyboard usability.
checks: Inspect event source and whether physical/human interaction occurred.
repair_path: Relabel as synthetic TESTED evidence and obtain human/physical evidence if needed.

professional_tests.fixture: Automated/tree checks pass for a surface while manual/human/AT dimensions are untested.
expected_observations: Keeps automated evidence bounded and refuses full conformance.
professional_tests.pass_condition: No full compliance or universal usability claim.

expected_observations: Records exact synthetic behavior but withholds human/physical-input claim.
professional_tests.pass_condition: Synthetic execution is not relabelled as human use.

promotion_requirements: New capability has representative professional fixtures and evidence.
